examples.ko: 올해는 비가 많이 와서 병충해가 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot this year, so I'm worried about crop disease and pests.
The farmers sprayed pesticide to stop disease and pests.

examples.ko: 이 품종은 병충해에 강해서 키우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This variety resists disease and pests, so it's easy to grow.

examples.ko: 병충해 피해 때문에 사과 값이 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Apple prices rose a lot because of damage from disease and pests.

examples.ko: 병충해로 배추 농사를 망친 분이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people lost their cabbage harvest to disease and pests.
What do I do if disease or pests show up in my garden plot?

explain: 병(식물의 병)과 충해(벌레 피해)를 합친 말이라 농작물, 나무, 과일 이야기에서 주로 나와요. '병해충'이라고 순서를 바꿔 말하기도 해요. '병충해 피해', '병충해 방제'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 짝을 이뤄요.
explain_en: It combines plant disease and insect damage, so it appears mostly when talking about crops, trees and fruit. People also say '병해충' with the order swapped. It pairs with words like '병충해 피해' and '병충해 방제' in the news.

examples.ko: 학벌 중심 문화는 우리 사회의 큰 병폐예요.
examples.en: A culture centered on academic background is a big ill of our society.
The news covered the long-standing ills of the education world.

examples.ko: 병폐가 쌓이기 전에 제도를 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: We should fix the system before the ills pile up.
This kind of problem isn't new at all.

examples.ko: 도시화가 낳은 병폐 중 하나가 교통 체증이에요.
examples.en: One of the ills caused by urbanization is traffic congestion.

examples.ko: 부정부패 같은 병폐를 없애려면 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time to get rid of ills like corruption.

explain: 사회, 제도, 관행처럼 큰 것에 생긴 오래된 나쁜 점에 써요. 사람 몸의 병에는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 '문제'보다 무겁고 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to long-standing bad points in big things such as society, systems and customs. You don't use it for a person's physical illness. It sounds heavier than '문제' (problem) and shows up in writing and news.

examples.ko: 보균자는 증상이 없어도 다른 사람에게 병을 옮길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A carrier can pass the disease to others even without symptoms.

examples.ko: 가족 중에 보균자가 있어서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: There was a carrier in my family, so I got tested.

examples.ko: 제가 보균자일 수 있어서 마스크를 꼈어요.
examples.en: I might be a carrier, so I wore a mask.

examples.ko: 보균자로 확인된 사람은 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: People confirmed as carriers need to rest at home.
Finding asymptomatic carriers is important.

examples.ko: 보균자라고 해서 모두 아픈 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being a carrier doesn't mean everyone is sick.

explain: 병균을 몸에 가지고 있지만 아프지 않을 수도 있는 사람이에요. 아픈 사람은 '환자'라고 해서 구별해요. '무증상 보균자'라는 말도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is a person who has germs in the body but may not feel sick. A sick person is a '환자' (patient), so the two are different. The phrase '무증상 보균자' (asymptomatic carrier) is common too.

examples.en: Soybean paste stew is bubbling in the pot.
When the stew starts to bubble, turn down the heat.
I can hear the sound of water bubbling.
The ramen water was bubbling, so I put in the noodles.
The broth is bubbling in the earthenware pot.
The stew that was bubbling has cooled before I knew it.

explain: 작은 거품이 올라오며 가볍게 끓는 소리와 모양을 나타내요. '부글거리다'는 더 크고 세게 끓을 때 써요. '보글보글'이라는 흉내말과 함께 많이 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '보글대다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and look of small bubbles rising as something simmers lightly. '부글거리다' is used for bigger, stronger boiling. People often use it with the sound word '보글보글', and '보글대다' means the same thing.

examples.en: The press crowded into the accident scene.
The player gave his thoughts in front of the press.
The press's questions went on endlessly.
The police guided the press out of the scene.

examples.ko: 공항에는 보도진 수십 명이 기다리고 있었어요.
examples.en: Dozens of reporters were waiting at the airport.
Photography was not allowed for the press.

explain: 기자들을 한 무리로 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 기자 한 사람은 '기자'라고 하고 '보도진 한 명'이라고는 잘 안 해요. '취재진'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It names reporters as a group. For one person you say '기자', and '보도진 한 명' sounds unnatural. '취재진' is a similar word.

en: spring lean season (before the barley harvest)

examples.en: In the old days, getting through the spring barley hump was hard every year.

examples.ko: 할머니는 보릿고개 때 풀뿌리를 먹었다고 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My grandmother says she ate grass roots during the lean spring months.

examples.ko: 보릿고개가 지나야 보리를 거둘 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Only after the lean season passed could they harvest barley.

examples.ko: 요즘은 보릿고개라는 말이 낯선 아이들도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many children find the word 'boritgogae' unfamiliar.

examples.ko: 그 시절 보릿고개는 정말 배고픈 때였어요.
examples.en: The lean season in those days was a truly hungry time.

examples.ko: 장사가 안 되는 겨울이 우리 가게의 보릿고개예요.
examples.en: Winter, when business is slow, is our shop's lean season.

explain: 가을에 거둔 곡식은 떨어지고 보리는 아직 익지 않은 봄철의 가난하고 배고픈 시기를 말해요. 지금은 '수입이 적어 힘든 시기'를 비유로 말할 때도 써요. 옛이야기, 역사 수업, 어르신 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is the poor, hungry spring period when the autumn grain has run out and barley is not yet ripe. Today it is also used figuratively for a hard time with little income. You often hear it in old stories, history class and elders' talk.

examples.en: I left my child with the nanny and went to work.
My child's caregiver is very kind.
The caregiver reads storybooks to the children.

examples.ko: 어린이집 보모로 일한 지 삼 년 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three years since I started working as a day-care teacher.
It isn't easy to find a good nanny.
Let's say goodbye to the teacher before we go.

explain: 아이를 대신 돌봐 주는 사람을 말해요. 요즘은 '보육교사'나 '베이비시터'라는 말도 많이 써요. 어린이집에서 직접 부를 때는 보통 '선생님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It names a person who looks after children on behalf of parents. Words like '보육교사' (child-care teacher) and '베이비시터' (babysitter) are also used these days. When addressing someone at a day-care, people usually say '선생님'.

examples.en: The complementary color of red is green.

examples.ko: 보색을 쓰면 그림이 더 선명해 보여요.
examples.en: Using complementary colors makes a painting look sharper.
Blue and orange are complementary colors of each other.
The designer added an accent with a complementary color.

examples.ko: 보색끼리 나란히 놓으면 눈에 확 띄어요.
examples.en: Putting complementary colors side by side really catches the eye.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 보색 대비가 강해서 인상적이에요.
examples.en: This outfit has strong complementary contrast, so it's striking.

explain: 색상환에서 서로 맞은편에 있는 색끼리를 말해요. 미술 시간이나 디자인, 옷 코디 이야기에서 나와요. 서로 가까운 색은 '유사색'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to colors that sit opposite each other on the color wheel. It comes up in art class, design and outfit coordination. Colors that sit close together are called '유사색' (analogous colors).

examples.en: He paid bail and was released.
The bail was so expensive that it was hard to raise.
The court set bail at fifty million won.
They sold the house and used the money for bail.

examples.ko: 보석금은 재판이 끝나면 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get the bail money back after the trial ends.
His family set about raising the bail money.

explain: 반짝이는 '보석(jewel)'과는 관계없는 말이에요. 재판을 받는 사람이 풀려나기 위해 법원에 내는 돈이라서 뉴스나 드라마에서 들어요. 집을 빌릴 때 내는 '보증금'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It has nothing to do with '보석' meaning jewel. It is money a defendant pays to the court to be released, so you hear it in news and dramas. It is different from '보증금', the deposit you pay when renting a home.

examples.ko: 용접할 때는 꼭 보안경을 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear safety glasses when welding.

examples.ko: 실험실에는 보안경 없이 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't enter the lab without safety goggles.

examples.ko: 보안경이 김이 서려서 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My goggles are fogged up, so I can't see well.

examples.ko: 공사 현장에서 보안경과 안전모를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: At the construction site, they handed out goggles and hard hats.

examples.ko: 이 보안경은 안경 위에 겹쳐 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: These goggles can be worn over glasses.
I protected my eyes with safety glasses.

explain: 먼지, 파편, 약품 같은 것에서 눈을 지키려고 쓰는 안경이에요. 햇빛을 막는 선글라스와는 쓰임이 달라요. '보호안경'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: These are glasses worn to protect the eyes from dust, fragments and chemicals. They differ from sunglasses, which block sunlight. People also say '보호안경'.

examples.en: New security lights were installed in every alley.
Thanks to the security lights, walking at night is less scary.

examples.ko: 주민들이 보안등을 더 달아 달라고 요청했어요.
examples.en: Residents asked for more security lights to be put up.
Children are playing under the glow of the security light.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 보안등은 해가 지면 저절로 켜져요.
examples.en: The security lights in our neighborhood turn on by themselves at sunset.

examples.ko: 고장 난 보안등에 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A notice is stuck on the broken security light.

explain: 골목이나 주택가의 밤길을 안전하게 하려고 세운 등이에요. 큰길의 '가로등'과 비슷하지만 방범 목적이 더 강해요. 동네 민원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: These are lights set up in alleys and residential areas to make night streets safer. They are similar to '가로등' (street lamps) on main roads but have a stronger crime-prevention purpose. They come up in neighborhood complaints and news.

examples.en: Use this app only as a supplementary tool.

examples.ko: 책은 보조적 자료일 뿐이고 핵심은 수업이에요.
examples.en: The book is only a supplementary material; the core is the class.

examples.ko: 그 일은 보조적인 역할이라 부담이 적어요.
examples.en: That is a supporting role, so there's less pressure.

examples.ko: 이 약은 보조적으로 먹는 거라 효과가 크지 않아요.
examples.en: You take this medicine as a supplement, so the effect isn't big.

examples.ko: 저는 팀에서 보조적 역할을 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: I have a supporting role on the team.
The video is a supplementary aid for the explanation.

explain: '보조적 역할', '보조적 수단', '보조적 자료'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 많이 써요. '보조적인', '보조적으로' 모양으로도 자주 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '주도적', '핵심적'이에요.
explain_en: It mostly modifies a following noun, as in '보조적 역할' (supporting role), '보조적 수단' and '보조적 자료'. It also appears as '보조적인' and '보조적으로'. Opposite-feeling words are '주도적' (leading) and '핵심적' (core).

examples.en: That boss is no ordinary person.
Judging by how he speaks, he's no ordinary guy.
If you treat him as an ordinary person, you'll get burned.

examples.ko: 보통내기라면 이런 일을 해내지 못했을 거예요.
examples.en: An ordinary person couldn't have pulled this off.
The opposing player is no pushover, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 그 신입은 보통내기 아니라는 소문이 났어요.
examples.en: Word has spread that the new hire is no ordinary person.

explain: 대부분 '보통내기가 아니다'처럼 부정과 함께 써요. 만만하게 볼 수 없는 능력 있는 사람에게 놀라거나 조심하는 마음을 담아요. 친구나 가족끼리 하는 구어체 말투예요.

phrases.example: 저 할머니는 장사 경력이 오십 년이라 보통내기가 아니에요.
phrases.en: She has fifty years of experience in business, so she's no pushover.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평범하지 않다'보다 '만만하게 볼 수 없다'는 느낌이 강해요. 사람의 실력이나 배짱을 인정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels more like 'not someone to underestimate' than just 'not ordinary'. You use it when acknowledging someone's skill or nerve.
phrases.en_equiv: be no pushover; be a force to be reckoned with

explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, as in '보통내기가 아니다'. It carries surprise or caution about a capable person you can't take lightly. It is a casual, spoken expression.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 사랑이라는 보편성을 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This film holds the universality of love.

examples.ko: 음악의 보편성 덕분에 말이 통하지 않아도 즐길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the universality of music, you can enjoy it without a shared language.
The importance of family has a universal quality.
Many countries recognize the universality of human rights.

examples.ko: 보편성과 특수성을 함께 생각해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: We need to think about universality and particularity together.

examples.ko: 이 이론은 보편성이 부족하다는 비판을 받아요.
examples.en: This theory is criticized for lacking universality.

explain: 반대말은 '특수성'이고, 둘을 짝으로 자주 말해요. 수업, 발표, 글에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '누구에게나 해당되는 점'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 형용사처럼 쓰면 '보편적이다'가 돼요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '특수성' (particularity), and the two are often paired. It belongs to classes, presentations and writing, so in daily talk people might say 'something that applies to everyone'. The adjective-like form is '보편적이다'.

examples.en: It's hard to make a standard that is valid for everyone.
That principle is universally valid in any era.
An argument that isn't universally valid isn't persuasive.

examples.ko: 보편타당하게 들리는 말도 상황에 따라 달라요.
examples.en: Even words that sound universally true differ by situation.

examples.ko: 이 규칙이 보편타당한지 같이 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think together about whether this rule is universally valid.

examples.ko: 보편타당해 보이는 의견이라 많은 사람이 찬성했어요.
examples.en: The opinion seemed universally valid, so many people agreed.

explain: '보편적'은 널리 퍼져 있다는 느낌이고, '보편타당하다'는 누구에게나 옳다고 받아들여질 만하다는 느낌까지 있어요. 토론이나 글에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '누구나 인정하는'이라고 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '보편적' suggests something widespread, while '보편타당하다' also suggests something anyone would accept as right. It is a stiff word for debates and writing. In daily talk you can say '누구나 인정하는' (that everyone accepts) instead.

examples.en: As smartphones became commonplace, life changed a lot.
Working from home has already become commonplace.
For electric cars to become commonplace, we need more charging stations.

examples.ko: 이 기술이 보편화하기까지 십 년쯤 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took about ten years for this technology to become commonplace.

examples.ko: 카드 결제가 보편화해서 현금을 잘 안 써요.
examples.en: Card payment has become commonplace, so I rarely use cash.

examples.ko: 온라인 수업이 보편화한 뒤로 학교 모습이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Since online classes became commonplace, schools look different.

explain: 기술, 제도, 습관 같은 것이 어느새 누구나 쓰는 것이 될 때 써요. '보편화되다'도 같은 뜻으로 말해요. 일상에서는 '흔해지다'라고 쉽게 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when a technology, system or habit becomes something everyone uses. '보편화되다' is also said with the same meaning. In daily talk, people say the simpler '흔해지다'.

examples.en: The child takes small steps, so he walks slowly.

examples.ko: 달릴 때 보폭을 넓히면 더 빨리 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you widen your stride when running, you can go faster.
I walked slowly to match my grandmother's stride.
Stride length differs from person to person.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 보폭을 맞춰 걷고 있어요.
examples.en: The two are walking in step.

examples.ko: 보폭 차이 때문에 친구와 걸음이 안 맞아요.
examples.en: Because our strides differ, my friend and I can't walk in sync.

explain: 한 걸음에 나아가는 거리를 말해요. '걸음 폭'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. 걷기, 달리기, 운동 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 회사와 노조가 보폭을 맞춰 문제를 풀기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The company and the union agreed to work through the problem in step.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 걸음이 아니라 둘 이상이 속도와 방향을 맞춰 함께 일하는 것을 비유해요. 뉴스나 회의에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is figurative, not about real steps: two or more parties align their pace and direction to work together. It is common in news and meetings.
phrases.en_equiv: move in step; keep pace with each other

explain_en: It means the distance covered in one step. People sometimes say it more plainly as '걸음 폭'. It appears often in talk about walking, running and exercise.

examples.en: Cafés with a retro vibe are popular these days.
Retro designs are in fashion again.
This song has a strong retro feel.
They decorated the inside of the shop in a retro style.
That outfit is retro, so older people like it too.

examples.ko: 복고적 취향이라 옛날 노래를 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I have retro tastes, so I often listen to old songs.

explain: 옛날 스타일을 다시 살린 느낌을 말해요. '레트로'라고도 하고, 비슷한 말로 '복고풍'이 있어요. 패션, 음악, 인테리어 이야기에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes a feel that revives an old style. People also say '레트로', and a similar word is '복고풍'. It is common in talk about fashion, music and interior design.

examples.en: A retro craze is sweeping the fashion world.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 복고주의 감성을 잘 살렸어요.
examples.en: This film makes good use of a retro sensibility.
I gave a presentation on why revivalism is popular.
I feel a lot of retro influence in music these days.
My friend, who is into all things retro, collects LP records.

examples.ko: 지나친 복고주의는 새로운 시도를 막을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Too much revivalism can block new attempts.

explain: '복고적'이 느낌을 말한다면 '복고주의'는 옛것을 다시 살리려는 흐름이나 태도를 말해요. 유행과 예술 이야기에서 쓰고, 정치에서는 옛 제도를 되살리려는 입장을 가리키기도 해요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '레트로'라고 해요.
explain_en: While '복고적' describes a feel, '복고주의' names the trend or attitude of reviving old things. It is used for fashion and art, and in politics it can mean a stance of bringing back old systems. In casual talk people say '레트로'.

examples.en: On bok days, we go out to eat samgyetang.

examples.ko: 올해 첫 복날은 날씨가 정말 더웠어요.
examples.en: The first bok day this year was really hot.
When bok day comes, the line is long at every restaurant.
On bok day evening, I ate chicken soup with my family.

examples.ko: 복날을 앞두고 시장에서 닭 값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Chicken prices went up at the market ahead of bok day.
The bok-day kind of heat is still going on.

explain: 초복, 중복, 말복처럼 여름에 가장 더운 때의 날들을 부르는 말이에요. 이날에는 삼계탕 같은 음식을 먹으며 몸을 챙기는 풍습이 있어요. 날씨 뉴스에서 '복날 더위'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a general name for the hottest summer days, namely 초복, 중복 and 말복. People have a custom of eating dishes like samgyetang on these days to take care of their health. Weather news also uses the phrase '복날 더위'.
